strengths: Several theoretical results about two-layer GCNs are obtained to compare with CNNs.
The whole paper is well-structured and problem is well formulated, especially both the training phases and generalization ability are discussed.
Detailed and quantitative explanation are entailed along with the arguments of this paper, also the explanation of the numbers are helpful in understanding such proofs with practical impressions.
Proof stretches are friendly to readers.

The paper treats all aspects of learning with regard to the proposed model. Namely, they derive a formula for the training process and for the resulting accuracy. Hence, the paper provides a complete theoretical analysis, which rigorously proves the benefits of GCN over CNNs (for the proposed data model). The paper is clearly written.
The motivation for analyzing why GNNs work theoretically is important and potentially inspiring for better GNN designs.
The formulation of the feature learning theory in GNNs is grounded and well-presented.
The simple simulation experiments are clearly shown.
weaknesses: The practical significance of the theoretical results is unclear, and the implications for real‑world applications are not adequately addressed.

The theoretical results do not fully capture the essence of graph structure information; they do not explicitly incorporate the adjacency matrix A and the Laplacian matrix L in a way that clearly demonstrates their impact on generalization.

The node feature part is far from reality, as there are no such golden methods to divide any feature into two orthogonal groups; more connection of the applicability of this node feature model to the real‑world setting is demanded, e.g., by showing some repression/clustering results of real‑world node features on such two orthogonal part.
Homophily, a key factor for GNNs and especially unavoidable for analytical works based on SBM, is not discussed; the paper focuses solely on the distribution of the node features.
Figures 3 and 4 should provide variance bars by repeating the experiments several times to show the stability of the results.

The model of the data is very specific and limited, even for a two‑class model; the two classes are modeled as some template signal and its negative, without noise that directly affects the signal, and the noise is supported on indices disjoint from the signal; the simplicity of the model and its motivation should be clarified.

The novelty of the proposed method seems limited; the main theory and proof closely follow the prior feature learning theory paper [1], appearing directly adapted from it, and the authors should summarize the main differences/contributions of this submission compared to [1].

The main results of why GNNs work are not surprising and do not add new insights to the community; it is well‑known that GNNs can help smooth the node features corresponding to the same class [2], so the results do not provide new insights or potential future topics.
The experimental results are also widely observed by previous work in the community.
